Key Highlights Anduril’s valuation has increased more than 250% from $8.5B in 2022 to $30.5B in June 2025 following their $2.5B Series G round (8x oversubscribed), which more than doubled the $14B valuation from August 2024. The company has raised a total of $6.26B across seven funding rounds from premier investors including Founders Fund (which contributed $1B in the Series G—its largest check ever), Andreessen Horowitz, and Sands Capital. The company doubled its revenue to approximately $1B in 2024.In 2025, Anduril secured several transformational developments: In February, the company assumed oversight of Microsoft’s $22 billion IVAS augmented reality headset contract with the U.S. Army (approved by the DoD in April 2025). In August, Anduril opened the first entirely new solid rocket motor (SRM) production facility in the United States in 50 years, positioning it as America’s third SRM supplier alongside Northrop Grumman and L3Harris. In November 2025, Anduril formed the EDGE-Anduril Production Alliance joint venture with UAE’s EDGE Group to manufacture autonomous systems in the Middle East, with an initial UAE order of 50 Omen autonomous air vehicles.With the U.S. defense market projected to reach $382.56B by 2030 and DoD’s FY2024 AI investment increasing 63.6% to $1.8B, Anduril’s focus on autonomous systems and AI positions it to potentially capture significant market share. The additional $9.3B allocated for advanced technologies further supports their growth trajectory.Anduril has strategically expanded beyond its core Lattice OS platform through acquisitions and new product development, including the Fury autonomous combat aircraft (2023), Dive-LD underwater vehicles, the Omen hover-to-cruise autonomous air vehicle (unveiled November 2025), and counter-drone systems backed by a $200M Marine Corps contract. In October 2025, Anduril acquired American Infrared Solutions (AIRS) to bring cooled-IR camera manufacturing in-house. The company also formed a strategic partnership with OpenAI in December 2024 to develop AI solutions for national security missions.The company’s Arsenal-1 facility in Ohio—a 5,000,000 square foot autonomous weapons manufacturing complex announced in January 2025—represents approximately $1 billion in investment and will create 4,000+ jobs when production begins in July 2026. Additionally, Anduril opened a solid rocket motor production facility in Mississippi in August 2025, investing $75 million plus $14.3 million from the Defense Production Act. The company is also establishing a 50,000 square foot R&D center in the UAE through its EDGE joint venture. This capital-intensive expansion demonstrates commitment to scaling operations**, with production capacity of 6,000 tactical rocket motors annually by the end of 2026.** Anduril Industries's Founding Founded in 2017, Anduril Industries emerged from a compelling vision: revolutionizing defense technology through Silicon Valley innovation. Palmer Luckey, the creative force behind Oculus VR, joined forces with Trae Stephens, a venture capitalist who recognized critical gaps in defense contracting. Together with CEO Brian Schimpf, former Palantir engineering director, they assembled a leadership team including Joseph Chen, a former paratrooper with Oculus experience, and COO Matt Grimm.The company quickly attracted significant investment, starting with seed funding from Founders Fund. Through multiple rounds, Anduril has secured $6.26 billion from prominent investors including General Catalyst, Valor Equity Partners, Andreessen Horowitz, and Sands Capital. Their latest Series G round in June 2025 raised $2.5 billion, valuing the company at $30.5 billion—more than doubling the $14 billion valuation from August 2024 and representing a dramatic increase from its $8.5 billion valuation in 2022. Founders Fund led the Series G with a $1 billion investment, the largest check in the firm’s history, and the round was 8x oversubscribed.At Anduril’s core is the Lattice operating system, orchestrating autonomous systems across air, land, and sea. By combining rapid technological innovation with deep understanding of government procurement, Anduril has positioned itself as a formidable challenger in the defense sector, breaking away from traditional contractor models through its focus on AI, robotics, and autonomous systems. What Anduril Industries Does: Core Products and Services Founded in 2017, Anduril Industries has redefined military defense by fusing advanced AI with autonomous systems. Their groundbreaking approach combines rapid technological innovation with deep defense expertise, delivering a comprehensive portfolio of next-generation capabilities to US and allied forces. From AI-powered command centers to autonomous drones and underwater vehicles, Anduril’s integrated solutions are transforming battlefield awareness and response.Lattice Operating SystemPowering Anduril’s defense systems is Lattice, their revolutionary AI-driven command and control platform. This sophisticated operating system processes real-time data from multiple sensors and assets, delivering instant battlefield awareness to operators through computers, tablets, and VR interfaces. By harnessing advanced computer vision and AI analytics, Lattice transforms complex battlefield data into clear, actionable intelligence. When a threat emerges, Lattice’s AI immediately processes information from radar systems, cameras, and other sensors across the battlefield. The system analyzes this data in real-time, using pattern recognition to identify threats and track movements. Operators can seamlessly switch between visualization modes – from broad situational awareness to detailed tactical views – enabling rapid, informed decision-making based on real-time battlefield conditions.Unmanned Aerial Systems (UAS)In the aerial domain, Anduril has developed a formidable fleet of autonomous systems. Their flagship Ghost UAS redefines aerial surveillance by combining advanced autonomy with helicopter-like capabilities. This versatile drone delivers extended flight times and superior maneuverability, enabling persistent intelligence gathering and reconnaissance across diverse environments. Expanding their aerial capabilities, Anduril acquired Area-I, bringing the innovative Altius series into their portfolio. These fixed-wing UAVs represent a breakthrough in deployment flexibility – their tube-launched design allows them to be launched from virtually any platform, from ground vehicles to aircraft in flight. This versatility makes the Altius series particularly valuable for rapid-response scenarios and distributed operations where traditional launch methods might be impractical. Anduril Industries also introduced Fury in 2023, a jet-powered autonomous combat aircraft developed through their Blue Force Technologies acquisition. This multi-mission Autonomous Air Vehicle (AAV) marks the company’s advancement into sophisticated unmanned aerial systems.In November 2025, Anduril unveiled Omen, a hover-to-cruise Autonomous Air Vehicle (AAV) developed in partnership with UAE’s EDGE Group. Omen combines vertical takeoff and landing (VTOL) capability with efficient cruise flight, packing the endurance, payload, and mission flexibility of much larger aircraft into a compact, runway-independent Group 3 platform. The system can be unpacked, assembled, and launched by a two-person team in minutes, with payload capacity described as three to five times that of traditional systems in its category. Omen builds on Anduril’s $850 million investment in mission autonomy technology and VTOL development.Counter CombatAnduril Industries has developed a sophisticated counter-threat ecosystem that integrates AI, autonomy, and advanced sensors to defend against evolving dangers. Their Anvil platform leads their counter-drone efforts with two variants: a standard interceptor that neutralizes small drones through high-speed kinetic impact at up to 200 mph, and the Anvil-M, equipped with explosive capabilities for engaging agile aerial threats. Both operate from mobile Launch Box bases and connect seamlessly with Lattice command software. This technology forms the foundation of their Counter-UAS Engagement System (CES), developed under a $200 million U.S. Marine Corps contract to enhance their integrated air defense capabilities. On the ground, Anduril’s Sentry Tower series employs AI-powered surveillance, with the Extended Range variant detecting threats up to 7.5 miles away and tracking autonomously beyond 5 miles.Complementing these systems is Pulsar, an AI-enhanced electronic warfare platform that provides electromagnetic spectrum control through jamming, geolocation, communications support, and IED countermeasures. Available in fixed, vehicle-mounted, and airborne configurations, with a portable version in development, Pulsar represents Anduril’s commitment to comprehensive defense solutions.Integrated Visual Augmentation System (IVAS)In February 2025, Anduril announced it would assume control of the U.S. Army’s Integrated Visual Augmentation System (IVAS) program from Microsoft, with the Department of Defense approving the contract novation in April 2025. The program, originally valued at up to $22 billion over 10 years, aims to provide soldiers with augmented reality headsets integrating night vision, thermal sensing, and real-time battlefield data from drones, vehicles, and other systems. Anduril’s Lattice platform had already been integrated into IVAS in September 2024, adding computer vision AI and enhanced situational awareness capabilities. Under Anduril’s oversight, software release cycles have been reduced from approximately 180 days to 18 hours. Microsoft Azure remains the preferred cloud platform for IVAS workloads, while Anduril focuses on software functionality and preparing to compete in the Army’s next-generation Soldier Borne Mission Command competition.Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUV)Anduril Industries is pioneering the next generation of autonomous underwater capabilities with two sophisticated vehicles: the Dive-LD and Dive-XL. The Dive-LD, a 3-ton modular platform with a 3D-printed exterior, excels in both littoral and deep-water operations up to 6,000 meters. Priced at approximately $2.5 million per unit, this versatile system can conduct autonomous missions spanning 10 days, focusing on critical tasks like underwater surveys, inspections, and intelligence gathering. Building on this foundation, Anduril developed the more advanced Dive-XL, an Extra Large Autonomous Underwater Vehicle designed for extended endurance missions. The system has already demonstrated its capabilities through a successful 100-hour continuous voyage test, with plans for an ambitious 1,000 nautical mile fully submerged mission in early 2025. Solid Rocket Motor SystemsIn August 2025, Anduril opened a full-scale solid rocket motor (SRM) production facility in McHenry, Mississippi—the first entirely new SRM facility in the United States in 50 years. The company invested $75 million of its own capital, supplemented by $14.3 million from the Defense Production Act. The 450-acre Mississippi Solid Rocket Motor Complex positions Anduril as the nation’s third SRM supplier alongside Northrop Grumman and L3Harris’ Aerojet Rocketdyne. By the end of 2026, the facility will produce 6,000 tactical motors annually, up from 600 previously. Over 700 motors have already passed static test firing. In April 2025, Anduril successfully completed two live-fire tests of its 21-inch hypersonic rocket motor for the U.S. Navy’s Standard Missile Program. The company manufactures motors using ALITEC, a proprietary aluminum-lithium alloy fuel formulation that increases range by up to 40%. Anduril acquired solid rocket motor company Adranos in 2023, gaining the Mississippi production site and establishing its entry into propulsion systems. How Anduril Industries Makes Money: The Business Model Anduril Industries is revolutionizing the defense technology sector with an innovative approach that sets it apart from traditional contractors. Rather than waiting for government contracts, the company proactively develops cutting-edge military technology using its own capital. This strategy enables Anduril to offer fixed-price contracts to agencies like the Department of Defense and Homeland Security, potentially achieving higher margins than the industry standard cost-plus model.The company’s impressive product ecosystem includes the Ghost autonomous drone series, Anvil counter-drone systems, Dive-LD underwater vehicles, and the sophisticated Lattice AI operating system that seamlessly integrates these platforms. This technological foundation, coupled with aggressive investment in innovation – reinvesting more of its revenue into R&D since founding – has positioned Anduril to target gross margins of 40-50%, substantially higher than the 8-10% typical of traditional defense contractors. Despite capital-intensive operations and complex defense regulations, Anduril’s innovative approach positions it as a market disruptor. The company’s Arsenal-1 facility in Ohio (5 million square feet, production beginning July 2026), Mississippi solid rocket motor complex (6,000 motors annually by end of 2026), and EDGE-Anduril Production Alliance in the UAE demonstrate its commitment to hyperscale manufacturing capacity. The company doubled its revenue to approximately $1 billion in 2024 and has secured transformational contracts including the $22 billion IVAS program assumed from Microsoft. Anduril Industries’s 2026 Valuation Anduril Industries’s 2025 valuation reflects diverse pricing inputs, including the company’s most recent funding round, current fund valuations, and secondary market transactions. Anduril Industries has emerged as a transformative force in defense technology since its founding in 2017, now standing as one of the sector’s most valuable private companies with a $30.5 billion valuation as of the company’s most recent funding round in June 2025. This latest milestone, achieved through a $2.5 billion Series G funding round led by Founders Fund (which contributed $1 billion—its largest check ever), marks a dramatic rise from $14 billion in August 2024 and $8.5 billion in December 2022. The round was 8x oversubscribed, and at approximately $1 billion in 2024 revenue, the valuation implies a 30.5x revenue multiple. The company’s fundraising prowess is evident in its total raised capital of $6.26 billion across seven rounds, consistently attracting premier investors like Andreessen Horowitz, General Catalyst, Sands Capital, Morgan Stanley, and Lux Capital. This strong financial backing has enabled Anduril to advance its innovative approach to defense technology, focusing on autonomous systems, artificial intelligence, and advanced sensor technologies. Anduril is now one of the 13 most valuable private companies in the world according to CB Insights, approaching half the market capitalization of established defense contractors like Northrop Grumman and General Dynamics. The company’s success stems from its product-centric commercial model and focus on fixed-price contracts, setting it apart from traditional defense contractors. Combined with its strong technological capabilities and growing market presence, Anduril has established itself as a pivotal player in the modernization of defense technology. CEO and co-founder Palmer Luckey, known for founding Oculus VR, brings invaluable experience in scaling breakthrough technologies. The leadership team includes veterans from Palantir, SpaceX, and leading defense contractors, offering a unique blend of Silicon Valley innovation and defense sector knowledge. This diverse expertise may enable Anduril to bridge the gap between commercial technology advancement and complex defense requirements. The team’s track record of successful exits and major government contracts demonstrates their ability to execute on both technical and business fronts.Disruptive Business ModelAnduril’s approach to defense contracting fundamentally challenges industry norms. By self-funding R&D and production, the company maintains control over intellectual property and development timelines, enabling rapid iteration and product improvement. The fixed-price contract model incentivizes efficiency and innovation, leading to accelerated development cycles and reduced costs for government customers. This approach has resulted in development timelines of 12-18 months compared to the industry standard of 5-7 years. The company’s estimated higher profit margins of 40-50% enable sustained investment in cutting-edge research and talent acquisition, creating a virtuous cycle of innovation and growth. Anduril’s business model also allows for more flexible customer relationships, enabling quick adaptation to changing defense requirements and market opportunities.Technological InnovationAnduril’s Lattice OS platform represents a fundamental shift in military technology integration. The system processes vast amounts of sensor data in real-time, enabling autonomous threat detection and response across air, land, sea, and space domains. Key technological achievements include advanced computer vision algorithms that can identify and track multiple targets simultaneously, AI-driven decision support systems that reduce operator cognitive load, and seamless integration with existing military infrastructure. The platform’s modular architecture allows rapid deployment of new capabilities without system-wide overhauls, ensuring adaptability to evolving threats. Anduril’s autonomous systems demonstrate unprecedented reliability in complex environments, with successful deployments in various weather conditions and operational scenarios.Business and Market GrowthAnduril Industries’ ascent in the defense sector is marked by strategic contract acquisitions and technological superiority. The company has secured pivotal partnerships with the U.S. Department of Defense, U.S. Customs and Border Protection, and key international allies. In 2025, Anduril assumed oversight of the U.S. Army’s $22 billion IVAS augmented reality headset program from Microsoft, formed the EDGE-Anduril Production Alliance joint venture with UAE’s EDGE Group (with an initial 50-unit Omen order), and partnered with OpenAI to develop AI solutions for national security missions. These relationships demonstrate Anduril’s ability to scale operations while maintaining product excellence. The company’s expansion into counter-drone systems, underwater capabilities, solid rocket motor production, and advanced surveillance networks showcases its adaptability to emerging defense needs and market opportunities.Vertical Integration and Manufacturing ScaleAnduril is executing an aggressive vertical integration strategy to industrialize defense technology production. The company is building Arsenal-1, a $1 billion, 5-million-square-foot autonomous weapons manufacturing facility in Ohio creating 4,000+ jobs, with production beginning July 2026. In August 2025, Anduril opened the first entirely new solid rocket motor facility in the United States in 50 years, positioning itself as America’s third SRM supplier with capacity for 6,000 tactical motors annually by end of 2026. The October 2025 acquisition of American Infrared Solutions (AIRS) brings cooled-IR camera manufacturing in-house. The November 2025 EDGE-Anduril Production Alliance establishes manufacturing capability in the Middle East. This manufacturing footprint enables Anduril to offer lower unit costs, faster iteration, and greater control over its supply chain than traditional defense contractors. Past performance does not guarantee future results, and all investing involves risk of loss.Although Anduril is well-positioned to disrupt traditional military contractors through its innovative autonomous systems and artificial intelligence capabilities, the company faces several material risks. As a defense technology provider primarily serving government clients, its success depends heavily on navigating complex regulatory frameworks, securing stable contract revenue, and maintaining technological advantages in a competitive landscape. Global conflicts can significantly impact defense spending priorities and create market opportunities, while simultaneously introducing operational challenges and supply chain volatility. Before investing in Anduril Industries, potential investors should evaluate several critical risks and challenges (the following examples do not encompass all potential investment risks): Government DependencyAnduril’s financial stability hinges on Department of Defense contracts, creating significant vulnerabilities. Budget cycles, political transitions, and changing military priorities can rapidly impact contract availability and value. The company must navigate complex procurement processes, lengthy approval cycles, and strict compliance requirements inherent to defense contracting. Congressional budget negotiations and shifting geopolitical priorities can create unpredictable funding environments, potentially disrupting revenue streams and long-term planning.Regulatory EnvironmentDefense contractors must navigate multilayered regulatory oversight across government bodies. Export regulations impose strict controls on international technology transfers and sales. Stringent cybersecurity protocols require comprehensive system security measures and certifications. Shifting policies and international relations can introduce new compliance requirements. Success demands meticulous management of intellectual property rights while maintaining essential security credentials and facility standards.Global EventsGlobal conflicts significantly influence defense spending and contract priorities. While ongoing conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East may increase defense budgets and demand for military technology, they also create market volatility and supply chain disruptions. Rapid shifts in geopolitical alliances can affect international sales opportunities and partnership possibilities. Peace agreements or de-escalation efforts could reduce military spending, while new conflicts might require quick pivots in technology development and production capabilities.Established Competitor AdvantagesTraditional defense contractors maintain substantial financial resources and long-standing government relationships developed over decades. Their established procurement channels, security clearances, and deep understanding of military requirements create significant barriers to entry. These incumbents can leverage their size to absorb cost overruns and invest heavily in competing technologies.Capital Intensity and Execution RiskAnduril’s aggressive expansion strategy—including the $1 billion Arsenal-1 facility, $75 million Mississippi SRM complex, and international joint ventures—requires substantial ongoing capital investment. While the company raised $2.5 billion in June 2025 and doubled revenue to approximately $1 billion in 2024, the timeline to profitability remains uncertain. Execution risks include scaling manufacturing operations to projected capacity, successfully integrating acquired companies and technologies, and meeting delivery timelines on major contracts like IVAS. The company’s assumption of the troubled IVAS program from Microsoft carries inherent risks, as the project has faced years of technical challenges and soldier complaints about previous iterations. The Future Outlook of Anduril Industries The defense industry stands at the cusp of unprecedented growth, with Anduril Industries strategically positioned as one of its fastest-growing players. The U.S. defense market’s projected expansion to $382.56 billion by 2030 reflects the increasing demand for advanced military capabilities amid rising global tensions. Anduril’s June 2025 valuation of $30.5 billion—more than doubling in less than a year—and its assumption of major programs like the $22 billion IVAS contract demonstrate its emergence as a serious challenger to established defense primes. This trajectory creates a fertile ground for Anduril’s innovative approach to defense technology.At the heart of Anduril’s competitive advantage lies its mastery of next-generation technologies. The company’s focus on autonomous systems, artificial intelligence, and sophisticated sensor technology directly addresses the military’s growing appetite for cutting-edge solutions.The Department of Defense’s substantial investment in emerging technologies further strengthens Anduril’s market position. With a planned $1.8 billion allocation for AI applications in fiscal year 2024—marking a 63.6% increase from FY23—and $9.3 billion earmarked for advanced technologies, the government’s priorities closely mirror Anduril’s technological expertise.Anduril’s strategic partnerships with defense contractors and government agencies, coupled with its expanding global presence, create robust pathways for market expansion. The November 2025 EDGE-Anduril Production Alliance establishes manufacturing and R&D capabilities in the UAE, with additional international expansion expected. The December 2024 OpenAI partnership and ongoing collaboration with Microsoft on IVAS cloud infrastructure demonstrate Anduril’s ability to work with leading technology companies. By maintaining its aggressive investment in research and development, particularly in AI, autonomous systems, solid rocket motor production, and cybersecurity, Anduril may be well-equipped to deliver integrated solutions that meet the evolving demands of military and security forces worldwide. The convergence of increasing defense budgets, technological advancement, and strategic partnerships may position Anduril to capture substantial market share in this rapidly expanding sector. Investors can either buy Anduril Industries stock via a pre-IPO broker like TSG Capital Advisors or invest in Anduril Industries indirectly through pooled investment vehicles, such as those managed by TSG Invest fund managers. When Will Anduril Industries IPO?As of 2026, it is unknown when Anduril Industries will go public. Executive Chairman Trae Stephens stated in June 2025 that while the company is not on a “rapid path” to an IPO, Anduril is “going through the processes required to prepare for doing something like that in the medium term.” The company’s $30.5 billion valuation and strong revenue growth (doubling to approximately $1 billion in 2024) suggest IPO readiness is advancing. While many investors anticipate an Anduril Industries IPO, it’s crucial to understand that an IPO is not the only type of liquidity event available for private companies. While much attention focuses on the possibility of Anduril Industries going public, other potential outcomes include acquisition or merger with another company. When evaluating an Anduril Industries IPO or similar venture-backed private companies, investors should also consider less favorable scenarios, such as the company remaining private or facing business challenges. Stay informed about updates on an Anduril Industries IPO and other potential liquidity outcomes. Additionally, investors typically have no control over share management, and the fund’s portfolio may include other holdings, potentially diluting exposure to Anduril Industries.
